newsitem.title: USA: Orange Cty board OKs restructuring plan, bond deal.
newsitem.headline: Orange Cty board OKs restructuring plan, bond deal.

text.p: The Orange County, Calif., Board of Supervisors on Tuesday backed plans to reorganise county government and refund nearly $200 million of taxable pension bonds.
Implementation of the restructuring initiatives could result in the reduction of about 241 full-time jobs and produce cost savings of about $11 million.

Orange County chief executive officer Janice Mittermeier first announced the reorganisation plan in June. It proposed the elimination of the county's General Services Agency and the transfer of its functions to other departments.

It also called for the elimination of the Environmental Management Agency and the transfer of its functions to other departments or to two new departments -- planning and development services and public works. The plans also outlined a new structure within the county executive office.

The county Board of Supervisors also adopted a resolution authorizing the tender offer of taxable refunding pension obligation bonds. The proposal calls for the county to sell about $200 million of debt to refund outstanding 1994 Series A pension bonds.
"They approved the tender offer today with the understanding that this is not their last opportunity to decide not to do this," county spokeswoman Diane Thomas said.
